sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Shelford’s Law of Tolerance**: States that the existence, abundance, and distribution of a species are determined by whether the levels of one or more physical or chemical factors fall within the range tolerated by that species.
• **Stenohaline/Stenothermal**: Organisms with a **narrow range of tolerance**; highly sensitive to environmental fluctuations (e.g., Coral reefs).
• **Euryhaline/Eurythermal**: Organisms with a **wide range of tolerance**; highly adaptable to environmental fluctuations (e.g., Salmon, humans).
• **Key Metric / Factor**: The 'Optimum Range' is the central portion of the tolerance curve where physiological processes are most efficient, while the 'Zones of Stress' lie between the optimum and the limits of tolerance.

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: Specialized niches, high sensitivity, low adaptability.

items.definition: Any environmental factor that restricts the growth, abundance, or distribution of an organism when it approaches the limits of tolerance.
The ability of an organism to modify its physiology or behavior in response to environmental changes, effectively shifting its range of tolerance.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Bio-indicators**: Using stenothermal species to monitor water quality or climate shifts.
• **Conservation Planning**: Identifying 'Climate Refugia' where environmental factors remain within the tolerance range of endangered species.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: Rapid climate change exceeding the rate of evolutionary adaptation.
• **Solutions**: Assisted migration and habitat corridors to connect fragmented ranges.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'Eury is Easy, Steno is Strict'.
• **Decoded Meaning**: Eury- (Wide/Easy to adapt), Steno- (Narrow/Strict requirements).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses 'Range of Tolerance' with 'Niche'. Remember: Tolerance is the physiological limit; Niche is the functional role + habitat.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Ecological Amplitude' to describe the range of tolerance in a professional, academic manner.

keyTakeaways: Species with narrow tolerance ranges are the first to go extinct under climate stress.
The 'Maximum Range' is defined by the lethal limits of environmental factors.
Generalist species (Eury-) are more likely to survive in rapidly changing anthropogenic landscapes.
